territorial_scope.description: Applies within Nebraska; reaches persons outside the state that conduct business in Nebraska or produce products or services consumed by its residents, and preempts political subdivision rules on personal data processing (Sec. 30).

evidence.quote: Conducts business in this state or produces a product or service consumed by residents of this state

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: LB1074, approved April 17, 2024, enacts the Nebraska Data Privacy Act, giving Nebraska consumers rights over personal data and imposing controller and processor duties on non-small businesses, enforced by the Attorney General through civil penalties.
summary.long: LB1074, approved April 17, 2024, adopts the Nebraska Data Privacy Act (Secs. 1–30) and conforming changes to other banking and finance statutes. It applies to persons doing business in Nebraska or serving its residents that process or sell personal data and are not small businesses; state agencies, financial institutions, HIPAA covered entities, nonprofits, higher education and certain utilities are excluded. Consumers may access, correct, delete and port personal data and opt out of targeted advertising, sales and certain profiling. Controllers must respond within 45 days, give privacy notices, limit collection, secure data, obtain consent for sensitive data, conduct data protection assessments for defined high-risk processing, and avoid discrimination against consumers exercising rights; processors act under contract. The Attorney General has exclusive enforcement authority, must give 30 days' notice and an opportunity to cure, and may seek civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation. No private right of action is created; local ordinances on personal data processing are preempted.

notes: Part 1 of 2 (Secs. 1-82, through 45-354). Amending sections show deleted and inserted text merged in this copy (e.g., 'January 1, 2024 2023'; 'five one thousand dollars' in Sec. 52; duplicated lettering '(i) (h)' and '(e) (d)' in Secs. 54-55), so inserted text cannot be separated reliably here; amendment rows rely on section headings. Sec. 3(1)(c) excludes small businesses, but Sec. 18 applies to them for sensitive-data sales. Sec. 29(1) refers to 'sections 26 to 29' including itself. The title says the bill repeals the original sections; no individual repeal is stated in this part. Federal references are fixed 'as existed on January 1, 2024'. Some amended Chapter 8 sections are not tied to a named act in this part. Part 2 covers Sec. 82 (opening fragment) through Sec. 105. Amended statutes are restated in full; per the amending-act rule, only changed text is coded, so restated text informs relations only. Sections 45-737, 45-905.01, 45-912, 45-1005, 45-1018, 45-1033.01, 77-2341, 81-118.01, 59-1722, 69-2103, 69-2104, 69-2112, 71-605.02, 71-612, 71-616, 84-712.05 and 4A-108 are both amended here and repealed as originals in Sec. 102-104. Sec. 97 cross-refers to section 13-609, which Sec. 103 repeals. Sec. 84(7) refers to subsection (1) (5), an apparent typo in the text. Sec. 100 sets Sec. 96 and 97 operative three calendar months after adjournment and Sec. 93-95 and 98 operative January 1, 2025. The section number for the part 2 opening fragment is inferred from context. Target instrument IDs are empty because no listed target is in the registry.
